title: Shadow Peckul
text: “Well, I’ll just say it—there was a mountain of stuff on my computer that would’ve been trouble if a girl ever saw it. Games, doujinshi data, you name it… Thinking about it now, I guess that counts as lingering attachment to Japan. At the very least, I wish someone would just delete it for me.”
Oh… unlike when Father couldn’t escape his false accusations, this time there wasn’t a trace of panic in his reaction.
“What surprises me more is that Raphtalia-chan can even use a computer. Aren’t those things hard to figure out the first time?”

“Well, this world does have communication devices like the video crystals, you know. And with Status Magic and things like that, if you’re used to that sort of interface, a computer isn’t so different.”
“Ahh…” Father nodded along at Itsuki’s remark.
“Maybe, in some ways, this other world is actually more technologically advanced than ours.”
“I mean, if you want to fly freely, there’s always magic, or you could just ride a flying monster. By the way, Naofumi-san, since it’s just us here—what kind of, uh, adult images were on there?”
“I don’t think it’s appropriate to just casually tell two minors that right after summoning them… but if it’s just a general overview, I guess there was a bit of everything.”

Judging by how much Father seemed to know about “that sort of thing,” his tastes must run quite broad, I say. Speaking of which, I recalled the time in a previous loop when Father, cornered in Melromarc by his lust-crazed fiancée, came fleeing to me for help.
“Father must be shocked to learn he isn’t a lolicon after all.”
“I’d appreciate it if we kept that kind of talk to a minimum.”
Father answered awkwardly, scratching his cheek. According to Rival, his type was a reliable woman who could protect him.
“If anything, even we can tell Naofumi-san prefers older women.”
“That’s right. Which means, hearing just the overview, we can guess exactly what kind of things were on that computer.”
“Yes, maybe I should try guessing using my ‘Accuracy’ skill.”
The conversation had turned completely into teasing Father, I say.

“Could you two dial it back a little? Look, back in my world—my era—tsundere types and loli types were still pretty popular, and, well, without really meaning to… ah, wait, never mind! Oh right, I got some model parts after beating Lord of the Sea!”

Father abruptly cut off his own explanation and whipped out the parts. And so, we set about assembling the model… and wouldn’t you know it, all the parts came together perfectly. Click, click—we snapped them into place one after another. What emerged was… a coelacanth model, I say. According to my Spear’s Appraisal, it was identified as a model of the coelacanth Latimeria.
“I wonder what this model is for.”
“If it’s just a souvenir, I’m smashing it.”
“In games, stuff like this sometimes turns out to be important later, so it’s a little scary. Let’s just hope it comes in handy somewhere down the line.”
“A coelacanth, huh.”
“Naofumi-san, I was suddenly curious—can you even eat coelacanth?”
“Huh? I’ve never eaten one myself, but a university professor once asked me about it.”

Honestly, I have to wonder just what kind of circles Father moved in during his university days. Stories about him bringing back bizarre ingredients keep popping up out of nowhere. His part-time job history is similarly mysterious, I say.
“If I remember right, it’s got wax mixed in with the flesh, so eating it gives you diarrhea. There are fish like that—not suited for eating—so you’ve got to be careful.”
“I see…”
“There are also fish that, aside from poison, contain oils humans can’t digest properly.”
“Speaking of fish you can’t eat, pufferfish comes to mind. Though I imagine you could dissect one without much trouble, Naofumi-san.”

“Yeah, through biomagnification—the buildup up the food chain—the toxins get concentrated until they’re dangerous. Pufferfish poison is famous for that. You actually need a license to prepare it properly back home. Though in this world, since weapons can identify poison for you, dissection’s a lot easier. Ren, you could probably manage it too, right?”
“Did it once, at that cooking contest.”
I suppose with the skill built into Father’s kitchen knife, cooking becomes simple enough for anyone.

“Oh, and apparently coelacanth is supposed to taste really bland. Though—there’s that famous anime movie where the parents who turn into pigs eat from a drawstring pouch that’s supposedly made from a coelacanth’s stomach, so who knows how accurate that is.”
Knowing that story, it’s probably about people who do something selfish and end up turning into pigs, I’d wager.
“I see. So even if we did get our hands on a coelacanth, it probably wouldn’t taste very good.”
“I’m more impressed by Itsuki’s appetite, that he’d even think to eat a coelacanth in the first place.”
“I was just curious, that’s all… Anyway, which way should we go?”
“There was a pedestal underwater that looked like it could hold a lantern, so I already lit it.”

I had completely forgotten about that. Itsuki held out his hand to Father, asking for the lantern, and the two of us went back into our assigned room to light the pedestal. Just then, the floor right by the entrance we’d come in through on this level crumbled away, transforming into a staircase.
“Looks like that’s the way. Let’s go.”
“Yes… Things are gradually diverging more and more from the events we know from the game.”
“True enough. Either way, all we can do is keep moving forward. According to game knowledge… it’s the 100th floor.”
“Finally, the halfway point. I’d like to hurry up, get back to normal, and go home.”
“Same here.”

We’d been challenging this dungeon for quite a while now, I say. Upon reaching the 51st floor, we found ourselves walking through a coastal area—like some deserted island field. The monsters that appeared were kappa. When we defeated them with Illusion, they simply vanished into thin air. Next came a labyrinth-like area made of stone, half-buried in sand. We pressed onward, solving one mechanism after another as we advanced. Eventually, upon reaching another neat five-floor interval, a different kind of boss than before began to appear.
A black… Peckul-shaped figure—not Father, but something like a Peckul—a boss called Shadow Peckul, lunged at us wielding a hammer.
“Peeeeeeck!”
Its movements were faster than anything we’d faced so far.
“Whoa! Wait, doesn’t that weapon look familiar?”
Father, having deftly dodged the attack from the Peckul as it swung its hammer and leapt at him, spoke while eyeing the weapon.
“It resembles the hammer among the Seven Star Weapons. I see—so this is the kind of battle where we face shadows wielding weapons modeled after the Seven Star Weapons.”
“I figured we’d be facing bosses ahead of schedule based on game knowledge, but I wasn’t expecting this.”
“I’d like to finish this quickly, but… fighting something that looks like Father is unpleasant, I say.”

It was a shadowy Peckul-like figure. Since Father currently happened to be a Peckul himself, this made things rather awkward. Given that it was carrying a hammer, I suppose you could call this some kind of Hero Peckul, in a manner of speaking. Oh? For a moment I wondered if, in my mind’s eye, Big Sister might turn into a Peckul as well… No, that doesn’t fit. Her Raph-species form leaves too strong an impression for that. Perhaps it makes more sense to instead picture Panda as the Seven Star Hero of the Hammer. Honestly, I wish it would decide whether it’s a panda or a penguin. A panda-patterned penguin, perhaps?
“Hah!”
“Peeeeck—!?”

With a flash, Ren struck first, cutting down the hammer-wielding Shadow Peckul in a single stroke. With a faint whoosh, the Shadow Peckul dissolved into nothing. A glowing drop item was drawn straight into Father’s shield.
“Huh? Guess it’s not distributed to everyone?”
“Seems that way. Naofumi-san, did you get anything?”

“Yeah. There’s something called the Shadow Peckul Hammer—looks like a pretty high-performance drop. The description mentions something about it being a hint for drawing out the hammer Vassal Weapon’s true potential. And there’s a shield too—literally called the Shadow Peckul (Hammer) Shield—that unlocks a skill boosting the effects of allies’ weapons.”
“I see. The Seven Star hammer was originally a weapon managed by Shieldfreeden. That must mean the Shield Sacred Weapon has the power to draw out the hammer’s full potential.”

So, through the power of Father’s shield, the Seven Star hammer could be strengthened. Come to think of it, there was indeed some connection between the Seven Star hammer and the Shield Sacred Weapon.
“The problem is, there’s no one around who actually wields the hammer’s Seven Star Weapon.”
In this particular loop, neither Big Sister nor Panda had ended up as its wielder.
